newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude firms on Nigerian Bonny force majeure.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude firms on Nigerian Bonny force majeure.

text.p: Brent crude rose further on Tuesday as force majeure by Shell on its Nigerian Bonny crude liftings due to a dock support staff strike at the terminal added around 10 cents to the paper market.
June Brent was sharply higher, up 28 cents a barrel at $18.62 by 1221 GMT. The market closed 42 cents higher at $18.34 on Monday.
Brent CFDs and spreads also firmed further.
CFDs rose with next week's talked in the June Brent - 36 cents/-33 cents range while May 5-9 was quoted at -35/-32 cents and May 12-16 at -33/-30 cents.
May/June tightened sharply to -15/-12 cents from Monday's -23/-17 cents while June/July was set at -6/-4 cents compared with -12/-10 cents a day earlier.
Two CFDs, April 22-25 was traded at June Brent -42 cents, and an April 28-09 changed hands at June -35 cents and two June/July contracts were traded at -7 cents.
A May/June Brent was heard traded at -16 cents.
Traders said no physical trades took place early. Two Brent cargoes were due to pass down the paper chains on Tuesday.
In a quiet Mediterranean market Russian Urals was talked at Dated Brent -$1.10/-$1.05.
That was up from its earlier level of Dated Brent -$1.20/-$1.10.
At least three big early May cargoes of the sour crude of 130,000 tonnes each were on offer, traders said.
They said one cargo of 54,000 tonnes for April 25-27 loading was sold on Monday by a Russian company but no further details were available.

Traders said Syria's state oil company Sytrol claimed that one term lifter had accepted its asking price for Dated Brent -82 cents for Syrian Light for May, but other lifters were still hoping for a small discount.
"They (Syrians) claim that somebody has alreaduy accepted to pay (Dated Brent) -82 cents but I think there is still room for more negotiations," he said.

"Nobody understood yet who is the one who agreed and I think there is still hope yet for decreasing a little bit their (Syrians') price which is (Dated Brent) -82 cents. The whole thing will be settled very soon, in a couple of days may be," the trader added. --Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
